scope: Research only: identify photographed dining-room ceiling/columns and check whether they can be registered to existing ATS geometry. No UE bridge, project assets or model changed.
conclusion: The photographs support a white-painted exposed beam-and-slab ceiling with substantial internal columns, suspended linear luminaires, fans and exposed conduits. They do not establish an exact beam/column grid or a mapping to the current restaurant world coordinates. The existing three rear-edge columns are an earlier exterior-verandah reconstruction and must not be treated as measured dining-room columns.

same_room_visual_correspondence.confidence: High visual correspondence between the 2021 dry group photograph, 2023 flood-cleanup view and two small school dining photographs; this is visual inference, not a labelled architectural plan.

The 2023 flood view and school anniversary dining photo share a large reflective side wall and a blue hanging recycling sign; the school leaflet selfie shows a reverse-facing reflective-wall side.

observations: Two especially clear substantial interior columns are near image x610 and x895, with additional perimeter/support portions visible; this is not a whole-room count.
Beams run in more than one direction, visibly drop below the slab, and meet the columns. The ceiling is not one uniformly flat interior finish plane.
Linear fittings are suspended on thin supports below the soffit, with ceiling fans and visible conduit. Their full count and coordinates are unknown.

source_limits: The evidence file cites Lands Department textured 3D survey for footprint, roof and canopy position; it explicitly says geometric error can reach 2.5 m and does not establish an as-built measured plan.
Three storeys at 0, 4.2 and 8.4 m are model choices; the source does not establish exact dining-room soffit height or beam depth.
The script calls the 2.2 m-deep strip an observed exterior verandah and leaves room interiors unassigned.
The 0.26 m square repeated exterior columns are not proven to be the large mosaic-covered internal columns visible in dining photographs.
existing_geometry_audit.implementation_warning: Do not build a dining beam grid by connecting the retained u6/u12/u18 exterior columns, and do not infer six-metre internal spans from their procedural spacing.

edges_and_directions: C1 and C2 appear aligned in the direction receding toward W. A visible downstand beam follows that line and meets their heads.
At these column heads, another family of downstand beams crosses the receding beam family, extending sideways toward the L/R sides.
The two families form a visually rectangular/approximately orthogonal structural layout; a calibrated 90-degree angle has not been measured from this image.
The slab remains above the dropped beams. Linear lamps hang below the slab/beam level on thin supports, and ceiling fans also hang into the room.
do_not_infer: The partially seen narrow supports near W are not sufficient to establish a third free-standing column or the end of a complete row.
No supported total row count, transverse column row, equal spacing, wall offset or metric dimensions follows from this topology.
The full transverse beam endpoints are partly obscured; do not assert a complete uninterrupted wall-to-wall span without additional views.
Do not use the earlier rear-exterior-verandah columns as C1/C2 world anchors.
